newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab ministers trickle in for Mideast meetings.
newsitem.headline: Arab ministers trickle in for Mideast meetings.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers began arriving in Cairo on Friday for two days of talks on the Middle East peace process.
But the Arab League said the ministers would not officially discuss the Iraqi crisis, which is not on their agenda.

The ministers, save the Iraqi representative, will meet informally on Friday evening to discuss the future of peace talks between Israel and its Arab neighbours and then again on Saturday for an emergency Arab League meeting on the issue.
The 22-member organisation will also hold its routine six-monthly meeting but diplomats said proposed United States airstrikes against Iraq were bound to come up.
U.S. fighter planes and an aircraft carrier headed to the Gulf on Friday for widely expected attacks to punish Iraqi President Saddam Hussein for defying patrols of no-fly zones over his country.
Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf told reporters on arrival in Cairo that Baghdad alone was reponsible for safeguarding its people and vowed to stand firm against U.S. attacks.
"The protection of Iraq is the responsibility of its people and not the responsibility of any other country," Sahaf said. "We will repulse American threats."

Libya's Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani has already condemned the threatened attack. Asked whether Iraq would discuss the issue, Sahaf said: "I am here to take part in the regular discussion of the items on the agenda."
Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said Saturday's meeting was important.

"This is the first meeting after Israel's new government embarked on a media campaign to hide its anti-peace policy. Israel is trying to show that it is keen on peace while it is actually its murderer," Bouez told reporters.
Israel on Friday rocketed suspected Hizbollah bases in southern Lebanon, heightening fears that the Jewish state may launch a widescale military attack.
Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha, Tunisia's Habib Ben Yahia and Farouk Kaddoumi, the head of the PLO'S political department or foreign minister, have also arrived.
Others include Jordan's Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs Khaled al-Madadha and Omani foreign ministry representative Haitham bin Tarek al-Saeed.
